question: A network automation engineer must configure a Cisco NX-OS REST API on a Cisco 9000 Series Switch with these requirements: NX-API REST and the DME database must be enabled; the NX-API REST must listen for HTTP traffic on port 83; and the HTTPS certificate must be uploaded. Which configuration set must be used to accomplish these goals?
options:
feature nxapi
nxapi {tcp} port 83
nxapi certificate {httpscrt}
nxapi certificate enable

feature nxapi
nxapi {http} port 83
nxapi certificate {httpscrt | httpskey}
nxapi certificate enable
theory: The requirement to listen on HTTP (not HTTPS) means the port command must use the 'http' keyword — 'nxapi {http} port 83' — while still uploading both halves of the HTTPS certificate (cert and key together, {httpscrt | httpskey}) so the certificate is complete, and the certificate only actually takes effect once 'nxapi certificate enable' is explicitly run afterward. Omitting either the key half of the certificate or the final enable step leaves the setup incomplete even though 'feature nxapi' and the port are configured. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools) / (Cisco documentation / web research)
